item.title: #1 [0/100] Longitudinal viral load trajectories predict cervical lesion risk in women with persistent human papillomavirus infection: A prospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L

Authors: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70648
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43069728



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is central to cervical lesion development, but single viral-load measurements may not capture heterogeneous viral dynamics. This study characterized longitudinal viral-load trajectories among women with persistent infection and evaluated their associations with cervical lesions and incremental predictive value beyond baseline factors. METHODS: In this prospective cohort of 1502 HPV-positive women followed at approximately 6-month intervals, latent class growth analysis using actual follow-up time was conducted among 624 women with type-specific persistent infection. Associations between trajectory group and any cervical lesion (low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion [HSIL]) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression; HSIL was explored using Firth-penalized regression. Discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve analysis were used to assess incremental predictive performance. RESULTS: Of 1170 women with classifiable outcomes, 624 had persistent infection. Four trajectories were identified: low stable (39.6%), moderate declining (18.9%), moderate increasing (29.8%), and persistently high (11.7%). Any-lesion prevalence was 10.9%, 17.8%, 74.2%, and 90.4%, respectively (p < .001). Compared with the low-stable group, fully adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were 1.95 (95% CI, 1.02-3.74), 29.66 (95% CI, 16.75-52.51), and 124.29 (95% CI, 47.30-326.60) for the other groups, respectively. The persistently high group was also associated with HSIL (OR, 9.47; 95% CI, 3.18-33.09). The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) increased from 0.713 for the base model to 0.888 for both the simple longitudinal and trajectory models and 0.899 for the joint model. CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal HPV viral-load dynamics identified clinically distinct risk phenotypes. Moderate-increasing and persistently high trajectories were strongly associated with cervical lesions, whereas longitudinal information improved discrimination beyond baseline measurements. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

Authors: Lin J, Jun H
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70589
Published: 2026-Nov-28
PMID: 43104789



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify drug targets affecting oral cancer (OC) susceptibility via immune cell-specific gene expression, offering genetic evidence for OC precision immunotherapy. METHODS: Cis-eQTLs of 15 peripheral blood immune cells from the DICE database were exposures; two independent OC GWAS datasets served as outcomes. Significant cis-eQTLs were selected as instrumental variables. MR analyses used IVW and Wald ratio methods, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. Validated associations underwent Bayesian colocalization. Target genes were analyzed by GO and KEGG enrichment. We predicted repurposable drugs using DSigDB, and assessed target safety via PheWAS. RESULTS: In the discovery cohort, MR found 64 cell-gene pairs with causal links to OC (FDR < 0.05); 45 replicated with consistent effect directions in validation. Colocalization prioritized 29 immune cell-specific targets. Enrichment showed these genes relate to T-cell activation and immune response. Candidates included tofacitinib, 6-mercaptopurine, and ciclopirox. PheWAS detected no severe systemic pleiotropic adverse effects of these protein-coding targets. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating immune cell-specific genetic regulation and OC risk data, we identified 29 high-confidence causal targets and repurposable drug candidates. This study provides novel genetic foundations for precision immune intervention in OC.

Authors: Lee KA, Kim HS, Lee SH, Kim HR
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70586
Published: 2026-Nov-28
PMID: 43104780



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate long-term changes in salivary gland ultrasound (SGUS) in primary Sjögren's disease (SjD) and to identify baseline factors associated with SGUS progression. METHODS: This longitudinal cohort study included 42 patients with primary SjD and 21 controls who underwent baseline and follow-up SGUS after a median of 8.9 years. SGUS was scored using the Hocevar system; Power Doppler and unstimulated salivary flow rate (USFR) were assessed at both time points. Progression was defined as an increase in total Hocevar score of ≥ 3, and associated baseline factors were evaluated by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Median total Hocevar scores increased in primary SjD from 24.0 (IQR 18.0-31.0) to 32.5 (IQR 21.5-38.0; p < 0.001), while controls showed minimal change (6.0 [IQR 5.0-8.0] to 7.0 [IQR 5.0-10.0]). Progression occurred in 71.4% of patients with primary SjD versus 14.3% of controls (p < 0.001). USFR declined modestly in both groups without correlation with Hocevar score change. Baseline Hocevar score ≥ 14 was independently associated with progression (adjusted OR 16.13, 95% CI 1.76-147.51; p = 0.013). CONCLUSION: SGUS abnormalities progressed over long-term follow-up in primary SjD, and higher baseline SGUS burden was associated with subsequent progression.

item.title: #5 [0/100] First-in-human results of NKT2152 monotherapy, an oral HIF-2α inhibitor, in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma: an open-label, multicenter, phase 1/2 study.
item.dc:creator: Choueiri TK, Xu W, Msaouel P, Logan T, Hall E, Hauke R, Bilen MA, Zakharia Y, Falchook G, Gordon M, et al.
item.description:

Authors: Choueiri TK, Xu W, Msaouel P, Logan T, Hall E, Hauke R, Bilen MA, Zakharia Y, Falchook G, Gordon M, et al.
Journal: Nature cancer | DOI: 10.1038/s43018-026-01282-4
Published: 2026-Nov-27
PMID: 43104112



Abstract:
NKT2152 (imdatifan) is an oral, potent selective inhibitor of hypoxia-inducible factor-2α (HIF-2α), which accumulates with von Hippel-Lindau deficiency and drives clear cell renal cell carcinoma. This first-in-human study included phase 1 dose finding, phase 2 dose expansion and pharmacology substudies in heavily pretreated patients with advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma; 93% had International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium intermediate- or poor-risk disease. Primary end points were dose-limiting toxicities in phase 1 and objective response rate in phase 2. Secondary end points included safety, pharmacokinetics, progression-free survival, time to response, duration of response and overall survival. Sixty patients received eight dose-escalation regimens, including continuous and loading and maintenance schedules necessitated by the prolonged half-life of NKT2152. Sustained erythropoietin suppression confirmed HIF-2α inhibition. The maximum tolerated dose was not reached, and two regimens were selected for randomized expansion in 40 patients. Anemia, fatigue and hypoxia were the most common adverse events. The pooled objective response rate was 22%, the median duration of response was 28.6 months and the median progression-free survival was 9.2 months, with no notable exposure-related efficacy or safety differences. Lower baseline circulating kidney injury molecule-1 and early reductions correlated with higher response rates and prolonged survival, supporting kidney injury molecule-1 as a candidate response biomarker. This study met all prespecified primary and secondary end points. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05119335 .

item.title: #6 [0/100] GenAI for Head and Neck Tumor Board Decision Support: Blinded Comparison of Retrieval Augmentation.

Authors: Remer E, Hack S, Dobriyan A, Rabinovics N, Saleh N, Alon EE
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70530
Published: 2026-Nov-27
PMID: 43102898



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate large language model (LLM) performance in multidisciplinary tumor board (MTB) decision support for head and neck cancer (HNC). STUDY DESIGN: Blinded comparative study. SETTING: Single tertiary academic center using real-world tumor board cases. METHODS: One hundred de-identified HNC cases were transcribed from institutional MTB presentation materials. GPT-4 and GPT-5 outputs, generated with and without in-context guideline grounding (RAG) using National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) 2025 guidelines, were evaluated by five blinded fellowship-trained head and neck surgeons. Outputs were scored across five domains: staging accuracy, treatment recommendation accuracy, prognosis accuracy, guideline adherence, and overall clinical usefulness using a five-point Likert scale with predefined anchors. Mixed-effects regression models accounted for clustering by case and reviewer. RESULTS: All configurations demonstrated high performance, with composite scores >4.45/5. GPT-5 without RAG achieved the highest mean score (4.82), followed by GPT-4 without RAG (4.55), GPT-5 with RAG (4.53), and GPT-4 with RAG (4.45). Configurations without RAG outperformed those with RAG (Δ = 0.22, P < .001), and GPT-5 outperformed GPT-4 (Δ = 0.15, P = .008). Mixed-effects modeling confirmed a significant effect of model version (β = .17, P = .001), while RAG was not associated with improved performance (β = -.06, P = .25); a negative model-by-RAG interaction did not reach significance (β = -.13, P = .07). CONCLUSION: LLMs demonstrate strong expert-rated performance in HNC tumor board decision support. However, naïve guideline-based RAG was associated with lower performance, suggesting that poorly optimized retrieval may introduce irrelevant context in complex decision-making. These findings underscore retrieval design as a critical determinant of safe clinical AI deployment and reinforce the need for clinician oversight.

Authors: Lechien JR
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70520
Published: 2026-Nov-27
PMID: 43102896



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the treatment response of two similar populations of patients with laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPRD): those treated with alginate or magaldrate monotherapy and those treated with alginate or magaldrate in addition to proton pump inhibitors (PPIs). STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of prospectively recruited patients. SETTING: University hospital. METHODS: Consecutive LPRD patients confirmed by 24-hour hypopharyngeal-esophageal multichannel intraluminal impedance-pH monitoring were enrolled at two European centers between January 2017 and September 2025. Symptoms were evaluated at baseline and 1, 3, and 6 months posttreatment using the reflux symptom score (RSS). RSS symptom, sub- and total score timelines were compared between patients receiving PPIs combined with alginate/magaldrate and those receiving alginate/magaldrate monotherapy. The natural course of symptom variation was evaluated in an untreated patient cohort through two assessments performed 2 months apart. RESULTS: A total of 388 patients completed the evaluations, including 185 patients (110 females) treated with monotherapy (alginate/magaldrate) and 203 patients (123 females) treated with combination therapy (PPIs + alginate/magaldrate). Combination therapy groups reported faster heartburn, and sticky mucus relief compared to monotherapy (1-month posttreatment). From baseline to 3- and 6-month posttreatment, both groups reported comparable symptom reliefs, and reduction of otolaryngological, digestive, respiratory, quality-of-life, and total RSS. CONCLUSION: Adding PPIs to alginate or magaldrate monotherapy does not provide additional overall symptom benefit in LPRD patients over the short-term to long-term, although combination therapy may accelerate early relief of heartburn and excess throat mucus within the first month of treatment.

Authors: Lechien JR, Chen G
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70534
Published: 2026-Nov-27
PMID: 43102894



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prevalence and findings of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) in laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPRD). DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases. REVIEW METHODS: Two independent investigators conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) systematic literature search for studies reporting GERD findings in LPRD patients. Methodological bias analysis was conducted with 2 validated bias tools. RESULTS: Fifteen papers met the inclusion criteria (n = 2081 patients). LPRD diagnosis was confirmed with hypopharyngeal-esophageal intraluminal impedance-pH monitoring (HEMII-pH) in 13/15 studies, and dual-probe pH-monitoring in 2/15 studies. The mean GERD rate across studies was 31.3% (range: 23.4%-61.3%) based on various GERD criteria, which rarely aligned with the evolution of GERD diagnostic criteria over time. Cumulative analysis of gastrointestinal endoscopy findings showed that A-C esophagitis, hiatal hernia, and D esophagitis/Barrett's metaplasia were present in 42.5% (1.5%-37.6%), 19.4% (5.6%-42.9%), and 2.3% (0%-6.9%) of patients, respectively. Only 3/15 studies used contemporary GERD criteria and aligned with guidelines available at study initiation. Acid exposure time was abnormal (>4%/>6%) in 107/370 patients (28.9%). The HEMII-pH profile of LPRD patients consisted predominantly of nonacid hypopharyngeal reflux events (HREs) (mean: 0.5-16.0) and lower proportions of acid HREs (mean: 4.9-44.3), respectively. Significant heterogeneity existed across studies regarding LPRD/GERD diagnosis, inclusion criteria, and HEMII-pH settings. CONCLUSION: GERD may affect 31.3% of LPRD patients, with prevalence varying according to patient characteristics (overweight, hiatal hernia, and HRE patterns). Most otolaryngology teams did not follow GERD consensus criteria for prevalence estimation, and studies often omitted endoscopy findings and complications, limiting conclusions.

Authors: Scher M, Mills M, Lafreniere D, Grillone GA, Tracy LF
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70479
Published: 2026-Nov-27
PMID: 43102887



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To histologically evaluate the cutting effects of a novel 455 nm laser across a range of power and distance settings and to compare with a 10,600 nm fiber-based carbon dioxide (CO2) laser. STUDY DESIGN: Descriptive study. SETTING: In vitro. METHODS: Using the 455 nm blue laser, and 10,600 nm CO2 laser, a 300 µm fiber was secured at specific distances (range: 1-5 mm) from ex vivo bovine tongue tissue. The tissue was incised at a constant speed and varying power (5-20 W). Histologic specimens were stained for hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH). Incision depth and thermal damage were measured and compared across different wavelengths, power, and distances from tissue. RESULTS: At 5 W, the average incision depths were 0.448 mm for 455 nm laser and 0.643 mm for 10,600 nm laser (P = .087). At 10 W, average incision depth was 1.01 mm for 455 nm laser and 1.31 mm for 10,6000 nm laser (P = .090). Increasing power to 20 W increased the average incision depth for the 455 nm laser to 1.588 mm (P < .0001). Laser distance from tissue (1-5 mm) did not significantly impact incision depth. Thermal damage depth of the 455 nm laser averaged 0.470 mm versus 0.150 mm for the 10,600 nm laser (P < .0001). Power adjustments did not significantly alter thermal spread depth for either laser. CONCLUSION: The 455 nm laser demonstrated similar incision depths to the 10,600 nm CO2 laser at 5 and 10 W, with increasing depth at 15 and 20 W. The 455 nm laser averaged 0.32 mm greater thermal damage depth than the CO2 laser. Increasing power for 455 nm laser resulted in deeper incisions without a proportional increase in thermal damage, indicating potential use as a cutting laser.

Authors: Kim DH, Jang DW, Hwang SH
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70526
Published: 2026-Nov-27
PMID: 43102884



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This network meta-analysis was performed to compare postoperative nerve-related morbidities among anterograde dissection (AG), retrograde dissection (RG), and extracapsular dissection (EC) in surgery for benign parotid tumors. DATA SOURCES: A systematic search of PubMed, SCOPUS, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was conducted through January 2026. METHODS: Studies comparing AG (main trunk identification), RG (peripheral branch identification), and EC (facial nerve-sparing) were included. Outcomes of interest included transient and permanent facial nerve palsy, Frey syndrome, and greater auricular nerve injury. Pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated within a network meta-analysis framework. RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies comprising 3263 patients were included. Compared with AG, EC was associated with significantly lower risks of transient facial nerve palsy (RR 0.35, 95% CI 0.23-0.52), permanent facial nerve palsy (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.23-0.99), Frey syndrome (RR 0.20, 95% CI 0.13-0.30), and greater auricular nerve injury (RR 0.32, 95% CI 0.17-0.59). By contrast, RG showed a trend toward lower complication rates than AG, but these differences were not statistically significant across outcomes. Ranking analysis demonstrated that EC consistently ranked highest, followed by RG, with AG ranking lowest. CONCLUSIONS: EC was associated with substantially reduced risks of facial nerve palsy and other postoperative morbidities compared with AG, whereas RG did not confer statistically significant advantages. These findings support EC as a favorable surgical approach for benign parotid tumors; however, further high-quality randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these results.
